transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, what brings me in is... I keep getting these flashes that just hit me out of nowhere. It's like I'm right back in this crowded holding room, seeing a fight break out and hearing everybody get shoved up against the wall. It happens all the time now, even when I'm just, you know, standing at a pickup counter for work. I just keep seeing it.
Do these flashes seem to happen at random, or is there something that usually triggers them?

Honestly, I'm not really sure. They just seem to happen whenever. I haven't really noticed if there's a specific thing that sets them off. Like I said, I'll just be standing there waiting to pick up a delivery, and it hits me. So, yeah, it just feels pretty random to me.
How long do these flashes typically last when they happen?

I honestly don't know. It's hard to keep track of time when it happens. It might just be a few seconds, or maybe a minute or two... I really couldn't tell you for sure. When I'm stuck in it, it just feels like time kind of stops until it finally passes.
Do you find yourself avoiding places, people, or activities that remind you of the holding room incident?

Yeah, I definitely do. Um... I've actually been turning down night runs for work, and I take the long way around town now. I just... I can't make myself go anywhere near that detention building. I also really try to avoid talking about what happened with anyone. If I talk about it, or if I get anywhere near that building, I just start feeling like I'm right back in that room again.
Do you experience any physical sensations, such as a racing heart or sweating, when these flashes happen?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed my heart racing or sweating or anything like that. When it hits me, I'm just... so caught up in the memory of it. If my body is reacting, I guess I'm just not paying attention to it. But honestly, no, I haven't felt anything physical like that.
Are there any specific emotions or feelings that you experience when you think about or are reminded of the holding room incident?

I just feel... scared, mostly. Like this really deep sense of dread. If something reminds me of it, I just get this overwhelming feeling of fear, like something terrible is about to happen again. I guess I also feel a little helpless when I think about it. But mostly, it's just fear.
Do you avoid talking or thinking about the holding room incident itself, aside from avoiding the physical location or people related to it?

Yeah, I do. Like I mentioned a few minutes ago, I really try not to talk about it with anyone. And as for thinking about it... I mean, I do whatever I can to push it out of my head. If a thought about that room starts creeping in, I just try to distract myself or focus on my deliveries. I just don't want it in my head at all.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself when these flashes happen?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I've never felt like I was watching myself from the outside. When the flashes happen, I'm just... I'm right back in that room. I'm definitely in my own body, just feeling exactly how I felt then.
Do you ever feel numb or disconnected from the world around you when you're not having one of these flashes?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm pretty focused on my work most of the time, just trying to get through my deliveries. I don't really feel numb or disconnected from everything... just scared when those memories pop up. But otherwise, no, I feel pretty normal, I guess. Just stressed.
Do you often find yourself thinking that you're bad, weak, or inadequate because of what happened in the holding room?

No, not really. I mean, I don't think I'm bad or weak because of it. I know it was just a really messed up situation that I got stuck in. I just... I just want it to stop messing with my head so I can do my job. But I don't blame myself or think less of myself for it, no.
Have you noticed any problems at work or in your relationships with others because of these flashes or your efforts to avoid things that remind you of the holding room incident?

Yeah, it's definitely causing problems. I've already missed two shifts at work. And even when I try to work, I just... I don't feel safe driving the route or handling my deliveries because I'm just too shaken up and constantly on edge. It's affecting other stuff, too. I had to stop showing up for my volunteer commitments because I just can't keep it together around people right now.
Do you have trouble falling or staying asleep at night?

Yeah, I barely sleep at all right now. I'll... I'll maybe doze off for an hour or two, but then I'm up again. Usually it's from some dream about being back in that cell, or... or I'll hear a door slamming and just jolt awake. By the time morning rolls around, I just feel completely wrecked. It's a big part of why I'm too exhausted to even try driving my route.
Do you often feel easily irritated or have outbursts of anger?

Yeah, actually. My temper has just been... snapping lately, for no real reason. Like, the other day I completely blew up at dispatch over a minor schedule change, which I'd normally just roll with. And then I was playing pickup basketball and cursed out this guy just for bumping into me. Usually, I'd just shake that kind of thing off, but right now I just have zero patience.
Do you ever feel guilty about what happened in the holding room?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I didn't do anything wrong to end up in there, so... no, I don't really feel guilty. Just... mostly just scared and angry about the whole thing.
Do you often find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats, even when you're not in a situation that would normally be considered dangerous?

Not really, no. I mean, I get startled easily by loud noises, like I said before with the doors... but I wouldn't say I'm constantly looking over my shoulder or scanning the room for danger. I'm mostly just staying in my apartment anyway right now, so I don't really feel like I'm on the lookout for threats like that.
Do you try to avoid memories or thoughts about what happened in the holding room?

Yeah, I definitely do. I mean, I try not to think about it at all. I've even been turning down my usual night runs for work, and I'm taking the long way around town just to make sure I don't go anywhere near that detention building. If I get close to it, or if I even try to talk about what happened, it just... it feels like I'm right back in that room. So I just avoid it completely.
Have you noticed any other areas of your life, aside from work, being affected by these flashes or your efforts to avoid reminders of the holding room incident?

Yeah, it's definitely affecting things. I know we talked about work a little bit, but I've actually already missed two shifts completely. And when I do think about trying to work, I just... I don't feel safe driving or handling my deliveries. I'm just way too shaken and on edge to be doing it. 

And outside of that, I also stopped showing up for my volunteer commitments. I just can't really keep it together around people right now, so I've just been staying away.
How long have you been experiencing these flashes and avoiding things that remind you of the holding room incident?
It's been about a week. Basically, it started right after I was detained overnight... ever since I saw that assault happen in the holding area, it's just been like this.
